title: Disk write smoke validation
question: Can a restored gem5 full-system run perform sane disk-backed guest file IO on the current single-core lineage?
feature_claim: Restored gem5 full-system simulation can execute a guest workload that creates, fsyncs, reopens, rereads, and verifies a disk-backed file on ext4 while running with FDIP enabled.

why: The guest binary auto-created and targeted a path under /var/tmp rather than tmpfs.
The binary performed create/truncate, repeated writes, fsync(fd), parent-directory fsync, sync(), reopen, full readback, and byte-for-byte compare.
The saved branch trace contains many hits on the success-loop branch PC and zero hits on the failure-loop branch PC.
The validating gem5 run used FDIP and the same trusted branch-trace infrastructure already used elsewhere in QPoints validation.
known_limits: This is a single-workload smoke validation, not a concurrency or multi-file logging stress test.
The reread happens after flush and reopen, but not after a privileged cache-drop or remount.
This package validates in-simulation disk behavior, not persistence back into the base qcow2 image.
